name: Aaron Quinn

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I am with the independent Work Futures Panel. We have no ties to employers, AI firms, unions, parties or government, and your answers are confidential. What do you do at work?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I lead a metal stamping press shift. We cut and bend brackets for equipment makers, and I set the feed and inspect the first pieces after a die change. I have a two-year technical diploma, but a drawing does not tell you when a press starts vibrating differently. I am well paid for this job and the younger operators come to me when a run begins drifting.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What is life outside the press like?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My wife Priya teaches music, and we have two school-age children and a mortgage. We have roughly a year of expenses saved, and there are several other factories within reach. I sometimes use AI to turn a supplier manual into a checklist, then compare every safety point with the printed manual. I will try something new after other shops have shown it works, especially if it saves scrap without weakening the guard checks.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the team that a quieter AI future still needs a good first-piece inspection. If scheduling gets quicker, fine; the press must make the right bracket.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our present income covers the mortgage and a year saved gives us options. I like the pay and I can see the value in training the next setter, so I would stay on this shift.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep checking the first stamped brackets and teaching the vibration signs. I would put the bonus from any newly paid scrap-saving run into savings after our normal bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel calm. The work is familiar and a faster checklist does not change who checks the die.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What do you teach a new setter first?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Listen before reaching for the control. A press can tell you a bracket is drifting before the first-piece gauge catches it. Then stop it and measure, not guess.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you continue using AI checklists?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Sometimes, for organising a long supplier manual. I compare the steps to the printed lockout page before I let anyone use the checklist. The tool saves reading time but has no authority over a safety procedure.

say: I would **keep** careful first-piece inspection on each metal stamping run.
A **quicker** schedule cannot excuse a wrong bracket.
think: Our **wages** cover the mortgage and a year saved gives choices.
This **senior** press job still rewards my experience.
do: **Keep** checking stamped brackets after each die change and teaching vibration signs.
**Save** new scrap-saving bonus pay after normal household bills.
feel: **Calm** about familiar work and a secure present income.
S0.quote: A press can tell you a bracket is drifting before the first-piece gauge catches it.
fieldNote: **Aaron** leads a metal press shift and uses occasional AI checklists only after checking the printed safety manual.
The **household** has about a year saved and higher press pay that currently covers its mortgage.
He would **add** a newly paid scrap-saving bonus to savings rather than relabel the existing reserve.

steps.text: Keep inspecting first stamped brackets and teaching press signs
Save new scrap-saving bonus pay after normal bills

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the press team that better office software may change schedules before robots touch a die. If the plant brings in a handling robot, I want to see its guarded production results and the staffing plan.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My setting knowledge stays useful now, but a robot taking blanks in and parts out could reduce operator hours later. A year saved lets me wait for evidence; it does not mean I want a smaller lead wage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask to observe a full guarded handling trial and compare rejected brackets with our normal gauge records. If the plant offers paid supervised robot instruction with isolation practice, I would take a recognised training place when it fits my shift. After training, I would apply for a posted senior cell role only if its wage and hours meet our mortgage and school schedule.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy about my future hours, but interested in a tested tool. I want to see robot handling through a full press run before giving anyone a new safety responsibility.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What counts as proof to you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A complete shift, not a short demonstration with perfect blanks. I would compare scrap and guard stops with our own press records. I would ask the fitter how the arm is isolated before practising the controls.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the new senior cell role is not posted?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep my current wage and check posted press-lead jobs at nearby plants. There are plenty of shops, but each wage, shift and commute must work with the mortgage and school routine. I would apply only to a real vacancy.

say: I would **ask** for guarded trial results and written staffing terms.
**Office** AI arrives before later robot handling of metal blanks.
think: A **robot** may eventually reduce press hours despite my setting skill.
A **year** saved gives time but does not replace my higher wage.
do: **Observe** a guarded robot trial and compare rejected brackets.
**Take** recognised paid supervised robot training only if offered on workable shifts.
**Apply** after training for posted cell work only with mortgage-covering pay and school hours.
feel: **Uneasy** about later hours, interested in proven safe production.
S1.quote: I want to see robot handling through a full press run before giving anyone a new safety responsibility.
fieldNote: **Aaron** would observe a full robot trial, then train only in an offered recognised paid place with isolation practice.
He **keeps** training distinct from a posted cell-role application needing sufficient pay and school-compatible hours.
**Without** a suitable plant role, he checks actual local press vacancies against pay, shift and commute.

steps.text: Observe guarded handling trial and compare rejected brackets
Take offered recognised paid robot training with supervised isolation and workable shifts
Apply after training for posted cell role only with mortgage-covering pay and school hours
Check posted nearby press-lead jobs if no plant role and wage shift commute fit

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the crew that AGI can take over schedules in 2028, while capable robots feeding, setting and clearing the press around 2031 are the serious change. We should ask for a written transition plan now.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect many press shifts to vanish if robots can handle a full run and die change. My experience may keep me on a small team, but I cannot count on that. A year saved gives us time, yet losing this higher wage would put the mortgage and music lessons under pressure.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Priya and I would postpone the planned car replacement and set a monthly limit for extras. I would ask the plant for written redeployment and pay terms. I would apply for a posted local maintenance-cell job only if I get paid supervised isolation training and the wage, shift and commute cover our bills and school timetable.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about a large wage change. With savings and several nearby plants I can take measured steps, but I would not shrug off an expected loss of shifts.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you leave as soon as the AGI software arrives?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No. The 2028 scheduling change is not yet a robot running the metal press. I would keep the paid shift and watch for the actual handling installation. I would not resign on a date alone.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Could you take a lower-paid inspection job?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only after comparing the posted wage and hours with our mortgage and school costs. A nearby factory job may make sense only if its net pay after commuting covers the mortgage. A verbal offer would not be enough to move.

say: I would **distinguish** 2028 scheduling AI from capable press robots around 2031.
I would **ask** for written transition and pay terms.
think: I **expect** many press shifts to disappear after capable robots arrive.
A **year** saved gives time but lost higher wages would strain the household.
do: **Delay** the planned car replacement and limit extras.
**Request** written factory redeployment and pay terms.
**Apply** for posted cell work only with paid safe training and bill-covering wage shift and commute.
feel: **Anxious** about major expected wage loss, able to act with savings and local options.
S2.quote: A nearby factory job may make sense only if its net pay after commuting covers the mortgage.
fieldNote: **Aaron** expects hands-on press displacement around 2031, after 2028 AGI changes scheduling.
**Savings** and plentiful local plants support a measured search without erasing risk to a higher wage.
A **maintenance-cell** application requires a posted role, paid supervised safety instruction and sufficient net income after the commute.

steps.text: Postpone planned car replacement and limit discretionary spending
Request written redeployment and pay terms from factory
Apply for posted local cell job only with paid safety training and bill-covering wage shift commute

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell colleagues five years is enough to train press setters on a new cell if management pays for real practice. AGI changes schedules in 2031 and capable robots reach the floor around 2034.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I will be 51 at the robot date. The diploma and press experience help me understand the machine, but not the robot arm isolation. We have enough saved to consider a move carefully, not to stop earning.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would enrol in an offered recognised automation-maintenance course only if the factory funds it, keeps my paid shift hours and provides supervised lockout practice that fits school pickup. After completing it, I would apply for a posted local cell-maintenance job only if pay after commuting and its hours cover our bills. If no paid course place appears, I would search posted press-lead jobs nearby with workable wages, shifts and travel.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel cautiously hopeful, with some anxiety about whether the place and later job will exist. I can learn robot press controls once a fitter demonstrates them safely.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What skill would you practise first?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Stopping and proving the robot arm cannot move before opening the guard. I would want the fitter to observe me do it repeatedly on paid time. A diagram cannot substitute for that check.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the course is only offered after your shift?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask for a paid class at a time that leaves school pickup covered. An unpaid evening class after a full press shift would not be a sound way to learn safety. I would continue on the press and look at posted jobs if those terms are unavailable.

say: I would **ask** for a funded paid automation course with guarded practice.
**Five** years leaves time to learn before capable robots arrive around 2034.
think: At 51, **press** expertise does not prove robot isolation skill.
A **buffer** permits a careful move, but I still need paid work.
do: Enrol in **offered recognised training** only with funded fees, retained paid shifts, supervised lockout practice and workable school hours.
**Apply** after completion for posted cell work only with bill-covering net pay and shifts.
If **no** paid course, search posted press-lead work with suitable wage shift and commute.
feel: **Cautiously** hopeful about learning, anxious about whether paid places and jobs materialise.
S3.quote: I can learn robot press controls once a fitter demonstrates them safely.
fieldNote: An **offered recognised course** requires funded fees, unchanged paid shift hours, supervised lockout practice and workable school timing.
A **separate** posted cell-maintenance application depends on net pay after commuting and a workable shift.
**Without** a paid course place, he retains his press wage while searching posted local lead roles.

steps.text: Enrol in offered recognised funded course only with paid shifts retained, supervised lockout and school cover
Apply after completion for posted cell job only with bill-covering net pay and shifts
Search posted local press-lead jobs if no course and wage shift commute fit

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the press shop that ten years lets us test a proper training route before robots handle a die. I want named instructors and posted jobs as well as the new equipment.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I will be 53 when AGI changes schedules in 2036 and 56 when capable robots reach the press around 2039. Our children will be older and we have a year saved, but a senior wage still matters. I would rather move into maintenance through a verified route than guess at one.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep leading the press and take an offered recognised funded course on paid school-compatible hours only with supervised robot lockout practice. Once qualified I would apply for a posted local maintenance job if the net wage after commuting covers our bills and the shift fits home. Without a course place, I would apply for posted press-lead roles with adequate pay and workable shifts. I would add any newly paid scrap-saving bonus to savings after our normal bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel guardedly hopeful. A decade helps if the employer actually creates the paid place and the next job.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you teach the current operators during that time?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Yes. I would teach first-piece checks and what a changing press vibration sounds like. A robot may feed the metal, but the next setter still needs to know when a bracket is wrong.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: When would you turn down a maintenance job?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If the posted net wage after travel fell short of the mortgage and school bills, or the shift left Priya alone with every pickup. I would compare the numbers before applying. A maintenance title does not compensate for an unusable household schedule.

say: I would **ask** for named instructors, paid course terms and posted jobs.
**Experienced** setters should pass on first-piece and vibration checks.
think: At 53 in 2036, **schedule** work changes before hands-on robots.
At 56 **near** 2039, I need viable paid work if robots take press duties.
do: **Keep** leading the press while taking only offered funded paid safe training.
**Apply** after qualification for posted maintenance work with bill-covering net pay and workable hours.
**Without** a course, seek posted press-lead work with adequate wages and shifts.
feel: **Guardedly** hopeful about a decade, dependent on real paid places and jobs.
S4.quote: A maintenance title does not compensate for an unusable household schedule.
fieldNote: **Aaron** seeks an offered recognised funded paid course with supervised lockout and school-compatible hours.
He would **separately** apply for a posted maintenance job at viable net pay or pursue posted lead work if no course opens.
**Any** new scrap-saving bonus would add to savings after bills; the existing year of cash is not new saving.

steps.text: Take offered recognised funded paid course with supervised lockout and school hours
Apply after qualification for posted maintenance work only with bill-covering net pay and hours
Seek posted press-lead roles if no course and pay and shifts work
Save newly paid scrap-saving bonus after normal bills

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: The two-year picture worries me most because robots could take many press shifts around 2031. A paid safe course and a posted nearby job whose net wage meets the mortgage would give us a way through.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I did not ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: I want my children to see why measuring a bracket matters even when a machine cuts it. A press can tell you a bracket is drifting before the first-piece gauge catches it.

headlineQuote: I want my children to see why measuring a bracket matters even when a machine cuts it.
portrait: **Aaron** Quinn, 43, leads a metal stamping press and holds a two-year technical diploma with higher operator pay.
He and **music-teacher** wife Priya have two school-age children, a mortgage and roughly a year of expenses saved.
He **uses** AI occasionally to organise supplier manuals but verifies lockout against printed instructions before adopting it.
With **several** nearby plants, he accepts proven technology and paid practice while guarding the value of his senior wage.
He would **train** in an offered funded paid safe place, then apply for posted work with viable net pay and family hours.
biggestWorry: **Capable** robots around 2031 could remove press shifts despite his senior skill and year of savings.
whatWouldHelp: **Provide** offered recognised funded paid safety training and posted local jobs with adequate net pay and workable school hours.
